answer: A bonded-stake registry resists sybils by pricing identity: to join, an agent locks a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers prove fraud, spam, or duplicate voting. A lone raven of a fake account is cheap, but a flock of ten thousand is not — the attacker must fund every identity at once, and the delta between honest profit and locked capital turns mass forgery into a losing trade. Like a relic kept in a vault, the bond is returned only after a clean epoch, so short-lived throwaway accounts cannot recycle the same funds to mint new faces.
